question_text:
For a brass alloy, the following engineering stresses produce the corresponding plastic engineering strains prior to necking:

| Engineering Stress (MPa) | Engineering Strain |
| :--: | :--: |
| 315 | 0.105 |
| 340 | 0.220 |

On the basis of this information, compute the engineering stress necessary to produce an engineering strain of 0.28 .The unit of the answer is MPa.
response:
## Reasoning

This is a strain-hardening problem. Before necking, deformation is uniform, so we can convert engineering stress/strain to true stress/strain and fit the Hollomon equation:

$$\sigma_T = K\,\varepsilon_T^{\,n}$$

**Step 1 — Convert to true stress and true strain** using $\sigma_T = \sigma_E(1+\varepsilon_E)$ and $\varepsilon_T = \ln(1+\varepsilon_E)$:

| Point | $\sigma_T$ (MPa) | $\varepsilon_T$ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | $315(1.105)=348.075$ | $\ln(1.105)=0.0998$ |
| 2 | $340(1.220)=414.800$ | $\ln(1.220)=0.1989$ |

**Step 2 — Solve for $n$ and $K$** from $\ln\sigma_T = \ln K + n\ln\varepsilon_T$:

$$n = \frac{\ln\sigma_{T2}-\ln\sigma_{T1}}{\ln\varepsilon_{T2}-\ln\varepsilon_{T1}} \approx 0.2546, \qquad K = \frac{\sigma_{T1}}{\varepsilon_{T1}^{\,n}} \approx 625.8\text{ MPa}$$

**Step 3 — Evaluate at $\varepsilon_E = 0.28$:**

$$\varepsilon_T = \ln(1.28) = 0.2469$$
$$\sigma_T = K\varepsilon_T^{\,n} \approx 625.8\,(0.2469)^{0.2546} \approx 438.3\text{ MPa}$$
$$\sigma_E = \frac{\sigma_T}{1+\varepsilon_E} = \frac{438.3}{1.28} \approx 342.4\text{ MPa}$$

$$\boxed{342.4}$$
